about: FICTIONAL documents and queries for an engineering check of LexFlow's case search. Every name, place, date and fact is invented; nothing here is a real matter, judgment or citation. Each query lists the (document, page) pairs that answer it. 'lexical' queries share words with their answer; 'paraphrase' queries mean the same thing in other words. Written by the developer, so it measures plumbing and gross behaviour, not legal research quality.

documents.name: Rent recovery plaint.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. Plaint for recovery of arrears of rent. The plaintiff, Meera Kulkarni, owns a shop at 14 Lotus Lane, Nashik. The defendant, Vikram Shetty, took the shop on a monthly tenancy at a rent of Rs. 18,000 payable on the fifth of every month.

FICTIONAL. The defendant paid rent regularly until February. From March onwards he paid nothing, and by August the arrears amounted to Rs. 1,08,000. Reminders sent by the plaintiff on 10 April and 2 June went unanswered.
FICTIONAL. The plaintiff therefore prays for a decree directing the defendant to pay the arrears with interest at nine per cent a year, and for costs of this suit.

documents.name: Notice to quit.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. Legal notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. You are hereby called upon to vacate and hand over peaceful possession of the shop at 14 Lotus Lane within fifteen days of receiving this notice, failing which proceedings for eviction will be started.
FICTIONAL. The notice was sent by registered post with acknowledgement due on 20 August and was also delivered by hand to the tenant's manager, who refused to sign the copy.

documents.name: Written statement of defendant.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. The defendant denies that any rent is due. He states that the roof of the shop leaked throughout the monsoon and the plaintiff refused to repair it despite repeated requests.
FICTIONAL. The defendant spent Rs. 42,000 of his own money on waterproofing and claims that this amount must be adjusted against any sum found payable to the plaintiff.
FICTIONAL. The defendant further states that the suit is premature because no valid notice terminating the tenancy was ever served on him.

documents.name: Trademark opposition.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. Notice of opposition to application number 9988776 for the mark SUNCRISP in class 30 covering biscuits, rusks and bakery products, filed by Golden Grain Foods.
FICTIONAL. The opponent has used the mark SUNCRUST for biscuits since 2009 and holds a registration in class 30. The two marks are phonetically and visually similar and the goods are identical.
FICTIONAL. Sales figures annexed show turnover of Rs. 40 crore under SUNCRUST in the last financial year, establishing a substantial reputation in the market.

documents.name: Employment termination letter.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. Your services as senior accountant are terminated with effect from 30 September on the ground of unauthorised absence from duty for forty-two days without leave or intimation.
FICTIONAL. You will be paid one month's salary in lieu of notice together with gratuity and the leave encashment due to you, after you return the company laptop and identity card.

documents.name: Medical certificate.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. This is to certify that Mr. Arjun Pillai was admitted to City Care Hospital on 12 August with a fracture of the right femur after a road accident and was advised complete bed rest for eight weeks.

documents.name: Bail application.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. Application for regular bail on behalf of the accused, who has been in judicial custody for ninety days. The charge sheet has already been filed and no further custodial interrogation is required.
FICTIONAL. The accused has deep roots in the community, owns a house in Pune, and undertakes to attend every date of hearing and not to tamper with evidence or influence witnesses.

documents.name: Sale deed dispute.pdf
pages: FICTIONAL. The plaintiff seeks cancellation of a sale deed dated 3 January executed by her late father, alleging that his signature was obtained by fraud when he was seriously ill and unable to understand the document.
FICTIONAL. A handwriting expert compared the signature on the deed with admitted signatures and found significant differences in letter formation and pen pressure.
